definitions.explanation: Repeated complaints, mild scolding, or nagging about everyday matters. Composed of 小 (small) + 言 (words). Implies persistent, low-level criticism rather than a single serious reprimand. Often used to describe a parent's or boss's habitual complaints.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}に{小言|こごと}を{言|い}われた。
examples.english: I got scolded by my mother.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}の{小言|こごと}が{毎日|まいにち}{続|つづ}いてうんざりだ。
examples.english: I'm fed up with my boss's daily nagging.

examples.japanese: {部屋|へや}を{片付|かたづ}けないと、また{小言|こごと}を{言|い}われるよ。
examples.english: If you don't clean your room, you'll get nagged again.

notes:
USAGE:
{小言|こごと} implies repetitive, relatively minor complaints — the kind of everyday nagging a parent gives a child about chores or homework. It is milder than {叱|しか}る (to scold), which can be a single, serious reprimand.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小言|こごと}を{言|い}う (to nag, to grumble at)
- {小言|こごと}を{言|い}われる (to get nagged)
- {小言|こごと}が{多|おお}い (to nag a lot)
- {小言|こごと}が{絶|た}えない (the nagging never stops)
